name: Unity Park (Andinet Park)
summary: Unity Park is a 20-hectare park opened in 2019 inside the National Palace compound in Addis Ababa's Arat Kilo area. It combines historic palace buildings, a zoo and cultural exhibits.
details:
Unity Park was inaugurated on 10 October 2019 inside the grounds of the National Palace (Menelik's Palace compound) in the Arat Kilo district of Addis Ababa. It covers about 20 hectares.

The park includes a zoo with 37 mammal species, among them giraffes, zebras, cheetahs and African wild dogs, plus thirteen aquatic species and an aviary of indigenous birds.

Visitors can also see historical artifacts, including a throne of Emperor Haile Selassie. The park focuses on Ethiopian culture and history, and religious books in Amharic, English and Ge'ez are kept for research and study.

The park is described as part of Addis Ababa's beautification programme, known as Beautifying Sheger.
highlights: Zoo with giraffes, zebras, cheetahs and African wild dogs
Imperial-era artifacts including a Haile Selassie throne
bestTimeToVisit: Year-round. The dry season (October to May) is the most comfortable for walking outdoors.
gettingThere: In central Addis Ababa at Arat Kilo. It is roughly a 20–30 minute drive from Bole International Airport, depending on traffic.
tips: Buy tickets before you go. Payment options have been SMS, online via Ethio telecom, or the Commercial Bank of Ethiopia, which also sells tickets in person at the compound.
Opening hours have been reported as 9 am to 4 pm, six days a week, closed on Mondays for cleaning. Check current hours before visiting.
Abrehot Library, Friendship Park and the Ethiopian Science Museum are all close by and can be combined in one day.

name: Entoto Park (Entoto Natural Park)
summary: Entoto Park is a large recreational park on the forested slopes of Mount Entoto, north of central Addis Ababa. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed inaugurated it in October 2020.
details:
Entoto Natural Park officially opened on 10 October 2020 as part of the Beautifying Sheger project. Some sources give 30 September 2020 instead. It covers about 1,300 hectares on the southeastern slopes of Mount Entoto, at 2,600 to 3,100 metres above sea level.

At its opening, the park had sports centres, restaurants and cafés, horseback riding, an artificial lake, art galleries and children's playgrounds. Capital Ethiopia reported that coffee was served by Kaldi's and Tomoca and that about 12 service providers operated in the park.

Kuriftu runs a resort, spa and adventure park inside the area, with rooms and tents, stables, a go-kart track and jogging and cycling trails. Booking sites list rock climbing, hiking, biking and archery.

By 2022, state media described the park as fully equipped with indoor and outdoor facilities, including sports centres, a library, restaurants and coffee shops.
highlights: Eucalyptus-forested mountain slopes above the city
Horseback riding, cycling and jogging trails
Cool highland air and views over Addis Ababa
bestTimeToVisit: The dry season (October to May). It can be cold and wet at this altitude during the June–September rains, so bring a warm layer.
gettingThere: On Mount Entoto, north of central Addis Ababa. Booking sites give roughly 42–55 minutes by car from Bole International Airport.
tips: The park is 2,600–3,100 m above sea level, so expect cooler temperatures than in central Addis.
Activity providers inside the park, such as Kuriftu, set their own prices and opening times. Check with them directly.
The historic Entoto Maryam Church is nearby.

name: Friendship Park (Sheger Park / Friendship Square)
status: open — as of August 2026 (Phase I opened September 2020; Phase II opened October 2022)
summary: Friendship Park, also called Sheger Park or Friendship Square, is a roughly 46-hectare urban park in central Addis Ababa. It has an artificial lake, musical fountains and riverside recreation areas.
details:
Friendship Square, the first major piece of Sheger Park, was inaugurated on 10 September 2020, on the eve of the Ethiopian New Year. President Sahle-Work Zewde and Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed attended. China Communications Construction Company built it.

The park has an artificial lake, a gathering square, musical fountains that are lit at night, jogging tracks, botanical areas, restaurants and event spaces. Amhara Media Corporation puts its area at about 46 hectares.

Prime Minister Abiy inaugurated Friendship Park Phase II on 30 October 2022. It sits between Abrehot Library and the main Friendship Square and includes 1.2 km of riverside development. Facilities include a children's playground, a running track, volleyball, football and basketball areas, an ecological garden, a visitor centre, a picture gallery, a garden cafeteria, an observation tower and a wedding and events venue. It has parking for more than 325 cars.

In August 2026, the Prime Minister said the park had earned nearly 1 billion birr in its first four years from entrance fees, commercial services and facility rentals.
highlights: Artificial lake with lit musical fountains at night
Phase II riverside park with an observation tower and ecological garden
Children's play areas and sports courts
bestTimeToVisit: Year-round. Evenings are popular for the lit fountains.
gettingThere: In central Addis Ababa near the Prime Minister's office, Arat Kilo and Abrehot Library. It is roughly a 20–30 minute drive from Bole International Airport, depending on traffic.
tips: An entrance fee is charged, according to Amhara Media Corporation. Current prices were not confirmed.
Phase II has a wedding and event venue that can be hired for social events.

name: Addis Ababa Riverside Development Corridors (Entoto–Kechene and Entoto–Kebena)
status: partially open — as of June 2026 (Entoto–Kechene Medhanealem 9.6 km section opened June 2026; Entoto–Kebena 10.5 km section opened late June 2026; other sections under construction)
summary: A city-wide programme to rehabilitate Addis Ababa's rivers and turn their banks into green corridors with walkways, cycle paths and cafés. The first long sections opened in June 2026.
details:
The Sheger riverside project, part of Beautifying Sheger, aims to clean up Addis Ababa's rivers and build green corridors along them. An earlier description said it would run about 56 km from the Entoto forest to the Akaki River in the south of the city.

On 2 June 2026, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed inaugurated the 9.6 km Entoto–Kechene Medhanealem Riverside Development Project. It runs from the Entoto Qusquam area down to Kechene and has pedestrian walkways, walking and cycling trails, access roads and riverside cafés and restaurants built through public–private partnerships. There are also riverbank plots for strawberries, highland coffee, citrus and honey, and stone terraces built by Konso craftsmen to control erosion.

At the end of June 2026, he opened the Entoto–Kebena riverfront, about 10.5 km of corridor with flood protection, new bridges and green public spaces. Reports put the area of this section at 87.6 hectares and describe it as part of a much larger programme that is still mostly under construction.

The remaining sections are planned to continue toward Peacock Park and Bole.
highlights: Riverside walking and cycling trails from the Entoto foothills
Cafés and restaurants along the riverbanks
Riverbank coffee, strawberry and citrus plots
bestTimeToVisit: The dry season (October to May), when the trails are less muddy.
gettingThere: Within Addis Ababa. The opened sections start in the Entoto foothills in the north of the city and are reachable by taxi or ride-hailing.
tips: Only some sections are finished, and construction continues elsewhere in the corridor.
Combine the Entoto–Kechene section with a visit to Entoto Park.
confidenceNotes: The exact inauguration dates of the Kebena section vary between 25 and 28 June 2026 across reports. No individual riverside café or hotel could be confirmed by name. The total corridor length and area are given differently in different reports.

name: Adwa Victory Memorial (Adwa Zero Kilometre Museum)
initiative: Addis Ababa city project (Adwa Zero KM Project), inaugurated by PM Abiy Ahmed
status: open — as of November 2026 (inaugurated February 2024; opened to the public March 2024)
summary: A memorial and museum in Piassa that commemorates Ethiopia's victory over Italy at the Battle of Adwa on 1 March 1896. It marks Addis Ababa's 'zero kilometre' point.
details:
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed inaugurated the Adwa Victory Memorial on 11 February 2024, and it opened to the public on 16 March 2024. It stands in the Piassa area, between the statue of Emperor Menelik II and St. George's Cathedral.

The project started in 2019 and was delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic. The building has eleven blocks and five floors on about 1.5 hectares, and a bridge links it to the Addis Ababa Mayor's Office.

There are four entrances, one for each cardinal direction, leading to areas themed 'Heroes of the North', 'Heroes of the South', 'Heroes of the East' and 'Heroes of the West'. The design borrows from Aksum monuments and Lalibela architecture. Statues of Emperor Menelik II and Empress Taytu stand on the plaza near a fountain.

The complex also has a museum, meeting halls, an amphitheatre, a library, an art gallery and an exhibition centre.
highlights: Statues of Menelik II and Empress Taytu
Architecture inspired by Aksum and Lalibela
Next to St. George's Cathedral in historic Piassa
bestTimeToVisit: Year-round. The area is especially busy around Adwa Victory Day on 1 March.
gettingThere: In Piassa, central Addis Ababa. It is roughly a 25–40 minute drive from Bole International Airport, depending on traffic.
tips: The museum's website is adwamuseum.com. Check it for current opening hours and ticket information, which could not be confirmed here.
St. George's Cathedral and historic Piassa are within walking distance.

name: Ethiopian Science Museum (Ethiopia Museum of Art and Science)
initiative: Addis Ababa Riverside Green Development Project Phase II (Beautifying Sheger)
status: open — as of November 2026 (inaugurated October 2022; permanent exhibition opened June 2025)
summary: A dome-shaped science and technology museum near the National Palace. It opened in 2022 with interactive exhibits and a 3D dome theatre.
details:
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed inaugurated the Science Museum on 4 October 2022. It is a major part of the China-aided Addis Ababa Riverside Green Development Project Phase II and stands on Niger Street near the National Palace.

The building is a circular, 9-metre-high exhibition structure on a 6.78-hectare site, described as a 'ring of wisdom'.

Its dome theatre is a 3D cinema about 24 metres high that seats up to 200 people. Exhibition halls have interactive displays on healthcare, finance, cybersecurity, GIS, data analysis, manufacturing and robotics.

The Prime Minister inaugurated a permanent exhibition at the museum in June 2025.
highlights: Close to Unity Park and Friendship Park
bestTimeToVisit: Year-round. It is an indoor attraction.
gettingThere: In central Addis Ababa near the National Palace. It is roughly a 20–30 minute drive from Bole International Airport.
tips: Opening hours and ticket prices were not confirmed. Check locally before visiting.
Combine it with Unity Park and Friendship Park nearby.

name: Abrehot Library
initiative: Addis Ababa city project, inaugurated by PM Abiy Ahmed
summary: One of Africa's largest public libraries, opened in January 2022 opposite the Ethiopian Parliament. It is reported to open 24 hours a day.
details:
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed inaugurated Abrehot Library in early January 2022. Sources give both 1 and 2 January. It stands in Arat Kilo, in front of the Ethiopian Parliament building.

The four-storey building has about 19,000 m² of floor space and 1.5 km of shelving, enough for 1.4 million books. It can seat more than 2,000 readers at once.

Facilities include an outdoor Knowledge Garden, an online learning zone called Knowledge Springs, eight bookstores, a meeting room, a cafeteria and a children's reading area.

The library is reported to open 24 hours a day, including weekends and public holidays, with brief early-morning closures for cleaning.
highlights: Next to Friendship Park Phase II
bestTimeToVisit: Any time. It is an indoor attraction reported to be open 24 hours a day.
gettingThere: In Arat Kilo, central Addis Ababa, opposite Parliament. It is roughly a 20–30 minute drive from Bole International Airport.
tips: It is reported to open 24/7 with short early-morning maintenance closures. Confirm locally.
Friendship Park Phase II is directly adjacent.

name: Gorgora Eco Resort (Gorgora Project, Lake Tana)
initiative: Gebeta Lehager (Dine for Ethiopia / Dine for Nation)
nearestCity: Gorgora (Central Gondar), about 60 km south of Gondar
summary: A lakeside eco-resort on the northern shore of Lake Tana at Gorgora, southwest of Gondar. It was built under the Dine for Ethiopia initiative and inaugurated in July 2024.
details:
The Gorgora Project was launched under the Dine for Ethiopia (Gebeta Lehager) initiative. Its first phase started in March 2021, and the project's 4.2 billion birr budget was shared with the sister projects at Wonchi and Koysha.

Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed inaugurated the Gorgora Eco Resort on 13 July 2024. It sits on the shore of Lake Tana at Gorgora town, in Amhara Region.

Booking listings describe lakeside villas and cottages set in gardens, with lake-view rooms about a minute's walk from the water. One listing gives about 95 rooms.

Historic sites around Gorgora include the Debre Sina Maryam church and Emperor Susenyos's old palace. Listings put the palace about a 30-minute drive away.
highlights: Lakefront setting on northern Lake Tana
bestTimeToVisit: October to May, the dry season. The landscape is greenest just after the rains, in September and October.
gettingThere: Fly from Addis Ababa to Gondar, then drive about 60 km south to Gorgora. Allow roughly 1–1.5 hours by road.
tips: Book accommodation in advance. The resort is listed on major booking sites as 'Gorgora Eco Resort by Ethiopian Skylight'.
Ask the resort about boat trips on Lake Tana. These were not confirmed from sources.

confidenceNotes: The operator is unclear. A May 2024 report says Ethiopian Skylight Hotel manages the resort, while a May 2026 report says Roda Hospitality Group operates it. Fana describes the location as 'Lake Gorgora', but other sources say Lake Tana at Gorgora. Room count and distances come from booking sites. The ~60 km distance from Gondar is approximate.

name: Halala Kella Resort (Koysha Project, Dawro)
initiative: Gebeta Lehager (Dine for Ethiopia / Dine for Nation) — Koysha Project, Halala Kella cluster
nearestCity: Dawro Zone (about 500 km southwest of Addis Ababa)
summary: A hilltop resort inside the historic Halala Kella wall in Dawro Zone. It overlooks the man-made lake of the Gibe III dam on the Omo River.
details:
The Halala Kella cluster of the Koysha Project was launched on 21 February 2021 under the Dine for Ethiopia initiative. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed inaugurated the resort on 1 May 2023, after less than two years of construction.

The resort combines indigenous and modern architecture and has presidential and modern rooms. It overlooks the man-made lake of the Gibe III hydropower dam.

It lies within the historic Halala Kella wall, attributed to King Kawo Halala, which originally ran about 175 km through a landscape of the Omo River valley.

In June 2023 the resort was handed over to the South West Ethiopia Peoples' Regional State, which agreed with Paradise Lodges Resorts and Hotels Management to run it. A May 2024 report lists it among the lodges managed by Ethiopian Skylight Hotel.
highlights: Views over the Gibe III lake on the Omo River
Combine with Chebera Churchura National Park
bestTimeToVisit: The dry season (roughly October to May), when rural roads are easier.
gettingThere: About 500 km southwest of Addis Ababa by road, which takes a full day of driving. The nearest commercial airports are Jimma and Arba Minch. Ask the lodge about transfers.
tips: This is a remote area, so book accommodation and transport in advance.
Booking sites list the property as 'Halala Kella Eco Lodge'.

name: Chebera Churchura Elephant Paw Lodge
initiative: Gebeta Lehager (Dine for Ethiopia / Dine for Nation) — Koysha / Halala Kella cluster
nearestCity: Konta / Dawro area, Chebera Churchura National Park
summary: A villa-style lodge in Chebera Churchura National Park, which is known for its forest elephants. Prime Minister Abiy inaugurated it in December 2023.
details:
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed inaugurated the Elephant Paw Lodge in December 2023. Fana's report is dated 23 December 2023. It is part of the Koysha and Halala Kella cluster under the Dine for Ethiopia initiative.

The lodge is in Chebera Churchura National Park, in the Omo–Gibe basin between Dawro Zone and Konta. The area was a controlled hunting zone before becoming a national park in 2005 or 2006, and it has a significant elephant population.

Booking sites list one-, two- and three-bedroom villas, including a presidential villa, along with an outdoor pool, restaurant, bar and spa.

A May 2024 report lists it among the 'legacy lodges' managed by Ethiopian Skylight Hotel and says guests can see African elephants up close.
highlights: Wildlife viewing in Chebera Churchura National Park, including elephants
bestTimeToVisit: The dry season (roughly October to May) for easier road access and wildlife viewing.
gettingThere: Remote. Expect a long drive from Addis Ababa, roughly 500 km or more, via Jimma or the Dawro area. Arrange transfers with the lodge.
tips: Wildlife sightings are not guaranteed. Go with park guides.
Booking sites list check-in from 2 pm and check-out at noon. Confirm with the lodge.

name: Wonchi (Wenchi) Crater Lake Eco-Tourism Village
initiative: Gebeta Lehager (Dine for Ethiopia / Dine for Nation) — Wonchi-Dendi Project
summary: A developed eco-tourism destination at Wonchi crater lake, between Ambo and Woliso. It includes an eco-lodge and community guesthouses, and was the third Dine for Ethiopia destination to open.
details:
Prime Minister Abiy launched the Wonchi tourism development in March 2021. The project shared a 4.2 billion birr budget with Gorgora and Koysha and was built by China Communications Construction Company.

The Wonchi-Dendi Eco Tourism Village was inaugurated on 13 January 2024. The Office of the Prime Minister described it as the third destination completed under the Dine for Ethiopia initiative. The homes of 13 local farmers were prepared as guesthouses for tourists.

Wonchi is a volcanic crater lake between Ambo and Woliso. It has two islands, one with the ancient Cherkos (Kirkos) monastery, which visitors usually reach by small boat. Lukewarm springs southwest of the lake are believed locally to have healing powers.

The eco-lodge on site is managed by Ethiopian Skylight Hotel and listed as 'Wenchi Eco Lodge by Ethiopian Skylight' (also 'Wanchi Ija Eco Lodge').
highlights: Boat trip to the Cherkos monastery island
bestTimeToVisit: October to May, the dry season. Expect rain from June to September.
gettingThere: Roughly 130–155 km west/southwest of Addis Ababa by road, about 3–3.5 hours, via Ambo (about 28 km away) or Woliso (about 38 km away).
tips: Wonchi is a popular day trip from Addis Ababa, but staying overnight lets you hike and take the boat trip at a relaxed pace.
Ask locally about boat and horse hire to the monastery.

name: Beynouna Village (Lake Beseka, Metehara)
initiative: Gebeta Lehager / 'Bounty of the Basket' initiative (as ENA names it), inaugurated by PM Abiy Ahmed
region: Oromia Regional State (East Shewa / Fentale area)
summary: A resort village on the shore of Lake Beseka near Metehara and Awash National Park. It was built on old volcanic lava fields and inaugurated by Prime Minister Abiy in November 2024.
details:
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed inaugurated Beynouna Village in November 2024. ENA's report is dated 10 November 2024. The village sits on the shores of Lake Beseka near Metehara, close to Awash National Park, on land that was previously a landscape of volcanic remnants.

ENA reports that it has modern bedrooms and a lounge, a cinema hall, amusement facilities and a spa. Its traditional and modern architecture is surrounded by orchards and farmland with oranges, lemons, papaya and mangoes, and the site keeps chickens, camels, cattle and goats.

At the opening, the Prime Minister noted the area's harsh climate and difficult landscape, and said Beynouna Village 'stands as a testament to the belief that anything is possible'.

The accommodation is listed on booking sites as 'Beynouna Village Eco Lodge', with air-conditioned rooms, an outdoor pool and on-site restaurants.
highlights: Spa, cinema hall and amusement facilities
bestTimeToVisit: The cooler months (roughly November to February). The lowland Metehara area can be very hot from March to June.
gettingThere: About 200 km east of Addis Ababa by road along the Addis–Djibouti highway, roughly 3–4 hours.
tips: Combine it with a visit to Awash National Park.
Book through the listed lodge in advance. Check current rates and amenities directly, since booking-site details vary.

name: Logo Hayk Resort (Lake Hayk, South Wollo)
summary: A resort at Hayk town in South Wollo, built under the Dine for Generations initiative and inaugurated in February 2026. It is the second 'Dine' project in Amhara Region, after Gorgora.
details:
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed reviewed progress on the Logo Hayk project at Hayk town, South Wollo Zone, in mid-2024. The aim was to make Wollo and the surrounding areas a tourist destination.

The resort was officially inaugurated on 7 February 2026 under the Dine for Generations initiative. The Prime Minister called it the second Dine project in Amhara Region, after Gorgora, and described it as built through a government–private sector partnership.

ENA reports that the resort covers 13.3 hectares and has several restaurants, swimming pools, internal asphalt roads, a helipad, fruit orchards and landscaped grounds.

Lake Hayk (Hayq) is a freshwater lake north of Dessie in South Wollo. The historic Istifanos monastery stands on its western shore.
bestTimeToVisit: October to May, the dry season.
gettingThere: Fly from Addis Ababa to Kombolcha (serving Dessie), then drive north to Hayk, roughly 1 hour. By road from Addis Ababa it is a long day's drive of roughly 400+ km.
tips: The resort opened recently, so confirm booking channels and services directly.
Combine it with Dessie and the Istifanos monastery.

name: Denbi Eco Lodge
region: South West Ethiopia Peoples' Region (Bench Sheko Zone)

details:
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed laid the foundation stone for the Denbi Lake Lodge as part of Dine for Generations and inaugurated the Denbi Eco Lodge on 18 January 2026. The PMO describes it as the first completed destination under the initiative.

The lodge is in Bench Sheko Zone, near Mizan Aman, on a 36.7-hectare site of forest and natural scenery. It was built with locally sourced materials and local expertise.

The launch introduced a timeshare ownership model for Ethiopians.

Booking listings mention an outdoor pool, villas and lake-view rooms. Bebeka, Ethiopia's largest and oldest coffee plantation, is about 28 km southwest of Mizan Teferi.
highlights: First completed Dine for Generations destination

tips: Confirm booking details directly, because star ratings and amenity details differ between listings.

name: Shabeely Resort
summary: A 385-hectare resort about 29 km from Jigjiga, designed to reflect Somali heritage. It was inaugurated in January 2026 with the presidents of Somalia and Djibouti in attendance.
details:
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed inaugurated Shabeely Resort on 31 January 2026. Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, Djiboutian President Ismaïl Omar Guelleh and Somali Region President Mustafa Mohammed Omar attended. The name is also spelled Shabelley or Shebele.

The resort covers 385 hectares and is about 29 km from Jigjiga, the regional capital. Officials confirmed in early January 2026 that its first phase was complete.

ENA reports 51 completed rooms, three restaurants seating up to 400 guests, a cultural venue, meeting halls, children's play areas and 15.4 km of shaded walkways.

There is also a fruit park with about 10,000 trees and a camel park.
bestTimeToVisit: The cooler months (roughly November to February).
gettingThere: Fly from Addis Ababa to Jigjiga, then drive about 29 km to the resort.
tips: The resort is new. Confirm booking and access arrangements directly before travelling.

name: Niin Lee Palm Lodge
summary: A palm-oasis lodge in Afar Region built around the 'Blue Eye' natural hot-spring pool. It was inaugurated in March 2026 under Dine for Generations.
details:
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed laid the foundation stone for the Niin Lee Palm Spring Lodge on 28 October 2023, as one of seven destinations under the Dine for Generations initiative. He inaugurated it in March 2026, and ENA's report is dated 22 March 2026.

The lodge covers about 78,000 m². It has two presidential villas with private pools, twelve interconnected bedrooms and sixteen one-bedroom units.

Other facilities include dining venues, a reception complex, a conference hall, parking and a helipad.

Visitors can see the 'Blue Eye' natural hot-spring pool, two artificial lakes, fruit and forest trees, and walk a 3.2 km eco-tourism trail. ENA links the region to the discovery site of the hominin fossil 'Lucy'.
highlights: Afar Region heritage, including the 'Lucy' discovery area
bestTimeToVisit: The cooler months (roughly November to February). Afar can be extremely hot from May to September.
gettingThere: In Afar Region, northeast of Addis Ababa. The exact location and access route were not confirmed, so check with the lodge.
tips: Expect intense heat. Carry water and sun protection.

name: Arba Minch Conference Resort
summary: A 120-hectare conference and leisure resort at Arba Minch overlooking Lake Abaya. It has a 1,300-seat conference hall and a floating restaurant on the lake.
details:
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed laid the foundation stone on 3 July 2023 on a 120-hectare site overlooking Lake Abaya, as part of Dine for Generations. He inaugurated the resort on 4 July 2026.

The resort has about 85 guest rooms, including two presidential suites, and a conference centre that holds more than 1,300 delegates.

Other facilities include floating restaurants on the lake, wellness facilities, landscaped gardens and cultural experiences. The architecture draws on Gamo vernacular design.

Arba Minch lies between Lakes Abaya and Chamo, next to Nech Sar National Park.
highlights: Lake Abaya and Lake Chamo scenery
Close to Nech Sar National Park
bestTimeToVisit: The dry seasons (roughly December to February and June to August are commonly drier in the south). Conference events run year-round.
gettingThere: Fly from Addis Ababa to Arba Minch Airport. Kana TV says the journey from Bole takes under two hours including the domestic flight.
tips: Combine it with a boat trip on Lake Chamo or a visit to Nech Sar National Park.
The resort is new. Confirm booking channels directly.
